normal_signature: Flexible, sealed foil or plastic packaging containing dry food products
Prominent printed branding, flavor text, and nutritional information labels
Visible barcode and QR codes on the packaging surface
Intact heat-sealed edges and crimped tops/bottoms
Background consists of a white perforated pegboard shelf
hypothesized_anomaly_modes: Structural breach: Tears, punctures, or unsealed edges compromising the vacuum or air-tight seal
Content failure: Visible leakage of food particles or liquid, or a completely deflated/empty package indicating spoilage or loss
Labeling defect: Missing, torn, or illegible barcode and nutritional labels preventing product identification
Severe deformation: Crushing or crushing that obscures the primary branding or suggests physical damage to the contents
rules: if the package shows visible tears, holes, or open seams then lean anomaly
if the package is completely deflated, crushed, or leaking contents then lean anomaly
if the barcode or primary branding is missing, torn off, or illegible then lean anomaly
if the package is standing or lying flat with intact seals and legible text then lean normal
if the package shows standard crinkling or inflation consistent with a sealed snack bag then lean normal

normal_signature: Rectangular prism packaging with sharp, well-defined edges and corners
Surface features high-resolution printed graphics, brand logos, and nutritional text
Packaging material appears rigid and maintains structural integrity without deformation
Background consists of a white pegboard with a uniform grid of circular holes
Boxes are positioned upright on a flat, reflective white surface
hypothesized_anomaly_modes: Structural deformation such as crushed corners, dented sides, or flattened faces due to mishandling
Surface damage including deep creases, tears, or peeling labels that obscure printed information
Sealing failure where the box flaps are open, unglued, or the packaging is visibly compromised
Contamination or staining on the packaging surface (e.g., grease, water spots, or dirt)
rules: if the box edges are bent, crushed, or the corners are rounded due to impact then lean anomaly
if the printed surface shows deep creases, tears, or missing label sections then lean anomaly
if the box flaps are open or the structural seal is broken then lean anomaly
if the box maintains a rigid rectangular shape with intact, sharp edges then lean normal
if the printed graphics and text are clear, flat, and free of physical distortion then lean normal

Sealed top rim with a standard pull-tab opening mechanism
Flat, stable base allowing the object to stand upright
Printed label wrapping around the body with legible text and graphics
Uniform curvature without visible dents or structural deformation

Corrosion or rust spots indicating material degradation or leakage
Label defects including peeling, tearing, or missing sections exposing the metal underneath
Damaged or missing pull-tab mechanism preventing the can from being opened
Seepage or liquid residue on the exterior surface indicating a breach in the seal
rules: if the object exhibits significant dents, crushing, or loss of cylindrical shape then lean anomaly
if the object is a rectangular carton or glass bottle instead of a metal cylinder then lean anomaly
if the top rim is missing, open, or the pull-tab is detached then lean anomaly
if the surface shows visible rust, corrosion, or liquid leakage then lean anomaly
if the object stands upright on a flat base with a smooth, intact metal surface then lean normal
if the label is fully adhered and wraps continuously around the cylinder then lean normal

Severe surface abrasion or scuffing that obscures the printed brand logo or health warnings
Peeling or flaking of the printed label layer from the cardboard substrate

if the brand logo or health warning text is heavily obscured by scuffs, stains, or peeling then lean anomaly
if the box maintains a rigid rectangular shape with a continuous, glossy surface then lean normal

Bottle resting on a white surface against a perforated pegboard background

Torn, peeling, or missing label exposing the plastic underneath
Severe leakage or spillage causing the bottle to sit in a puddle or appear wet

if the cap is missing, detached, or visibly loose then lean anomaly
if the label is torn, peeling, or completely missing then lean anomaly
if the bottle is lying on its side or tilted at an extreme angle then lean anomaly

if the background is a perforated pegboard and the bottle is centered then lean normal

normal_signature: Cylindrical or tapered cup-shaped container with a distinct lid
Surface covered in printed branding, nutritional labels, or graphics
Lid is sealed with a plastic film or foil layer
Container sits upright on a flat surface
Background features a white pegboard with a grid of holes

Seal failure: The plastic film or foil lid is torn, punctured, or missing, exposing the contents.
Label damage: The printed surface is significantly scratched, peeled, or obscured, making branding unreadable.
Foreign object contamination: Presence of non-package items (e.g., dirt, other food) on the surface or lid.
rules: if the container body is visibly crushed, dented, or bent out of shape then lean anomaly
if the lid seal is torn, punctured, or completely missing then lean anomaly
if the printed label is heavily scratched, peeled, or obscured then lean anomaly
if the container is a standard cup shape with an intact lid and clear graphics then lean normal
if the container is upright and the background is a pegboard then lean normal
